Recorded per n: min m(T) over W5 and W4 (top-12 minimisers), counts of delta<0 and delta=0 in W5/W4, per-k minima, per-alpha minima, the window-top (k=q) minimum, and the exact min Newton ratio r_k = delta_k (k+1)(alpha-k+1)/(alpha+1) (n<=28 enforced for __int128 safety). FLOAT tilted diagnostics were also taken: min V_k*delta_k binned by V. The Fang statistic Q_k = V^{3/2}(2p_k - p_{k-1} - p_{k+1}) was run exhaustively for n = 10..26 with central_margin_q.c. tilted_V_delta:
All values in this field are FLOAT diagnostics. lambda_k is the hard-core fugacity with mean exactly k; V_k is the variance there.

(1) V_k*delta_k over every tree with n<=27 and every k in W5 is at least 0.5122, reached at n=13 by a tree with alpha=7 at k=q=5, V=0.89. Per-n minima: 0.548, 0.516, 0.574, 0.512, 0.606, 0.637, 0.652, 0.645, 0.644, 0.649, 0.678, 0.712, 0.685, 0.712, 0.681, 0.718, 0.738, 0.748 for n=10..27. The minimum always sits at the window top k=q, in trees with small alpha where V is about 0.9-2.3 (the discrete O(1)-variance regime).

Restricted to V>=4, V*delta >= 0.81 for n=17..27 (0.8098 at n=26). In the families to n~300, the minimum of V*delta by V bin is 0.516 (V>=0), 0.705 (V>=2), 0.812 (V>=4), 0.896 (V>=8) and 0.942 (V>=16). At each family's delta-minimiser at the largest n, V*delta is 0.963-0.990. So V*delta -> 1 (delta ~ 1/V, the Gaussian value). The star at its argmin gives V*delta = 0.750 at n=10 rising to 0.895 at n=27 (-> (n-1)/(n+2)).

Samples (Bernoulli by a hash of the parent array; 2,099 / 1,992 / 1,992 trees at n=16/20/24) sit inside the exhaustive extremes: min V*delta 0.652 / 0.702 / 0.741, medians 0.714 / 0.764 / 0.800, min at k=q in 91/72/82% of trees, none below 1/4.

So V_k*delta_k is bounded below by about 1/2 on the central window in everything seen. That is well above the Poisson-binomial Theorem thm:main value 1/4, and above its bracket 1/4 <= c* <= 1/3 (paper/poisson_binomial/main.tex). The comparison is not like-for-like: that theorem uses the first descent of the untilted law with V>=1, while here k is the exact tilted mean.

(2) Fang et al. arXiv:2609.20961, Proposition 6.2, Eq. (6.4), p.11 (read from my own pdftotext extraction, sources/fang_2026.txt): sigma^3(2P(X=k) - P(X=k-1) - P(X=k+1)) -> 1/sqrt(2 pi) uniformly over forests on n vertices and lambda in K=[1/4,12] (K defined p.3), with mu=k. LC (6.5) then follows by AM-GM. Their p.3 overview says the mean is at most n/5 at lambda=1/4 and exceeds 17alpha/25 at lambda=12, so W5 lies inside their range.

Measured Q_k: Q_k > 0 for EVERY tree n<=26 and every k in W5 (0 trees with Q<=0), so their pointwise criterion never fails in the data, even at n=10. Min Q is 0.2116 at n=10 (star at the boundary k=2), 0.286 at n=24, 0.305 at n=25, 0.309 at n=26. With V>=4, min Q >= 0.332 (n=17..26). In the families, Q at the delta-argmin at the largest n is 0.387-0.396, against the limit 0.3989. Evaluated at each family member's Q-minimising k (not at every window k), (1/sqrt(2pi) - Q)*V <= 0.369, and in the exhaustive bins with V>=4 it is <= 0.28. So the observed convergence in (6.4) is O(1/V) with a small constant.

(3) The Newton ratio (exact) fails inside W5, but mildly. The min is 0.923-0.945 for 11<=n<=27 (0.844 at n=10 from the star's k=2 term, where i_1=n). At n=27, 4,841,128 trees (0.64%) have some r_k<1, and 58% of them fail first at k=q. The minimisers are star-of-stars shapes (a root joined to the centres of several K_{1,3}). The families' minimum is 0.883 (n=10), and the star-of-K_{1,3} family stays >= 0.917 to n=289.

(4) Hill-climbs, simulated annealing, 300 s each. Minimising n*m(T) at n=40 (1.66M exact evaluations) and n=80 (0.54M) converged to the star exactly and found nothing below it. Minimising Q over V>=4 at n=50 reached 0.354. The Newton-ratio climb at n=50 reached only 0.958, worse than the known family value 0.921 at n=49, so it is a failed kill-test for that objective and counts as no evidence.

scaling_hypothesis:
Two scales, kept separate. Evidence only, no theorem.

(A) On the delta scale: min over trees T on n vertices of min_{k in W5(T)} delta_k equals the star's value, 4/(n+2) for n even and 4n/(n+1)^2 for n odd, so n*min delta -> 4 from below. This holds exactly, with the star as unique minimiser, at every n from 10 to 27 (1.2e9 trees). No family member (0 of 473, n<=301) and no hill-climb (n=40, 80) goes below it. Near-star families approach n*m -> 4 from above; every other family has a constant between about 4.5 and 10.4. The same minimum holds on W4. This is the number an effective argument must beat: delta ~ 4/n. The extremal law is the binomial C(n-1,k), which saturates Newton's inequality.

(B) On the local-limit scale, the scale-free forms stay bounded away from zero everywhere seen. V_k*delta_k >= 0.51 overall, >= 0.81 for V>=4, and -> 1. The Fang et al. Prop. 6.2 statistic satisfies Q_k >= 0.21 overall, >= 0.33 for V>=4, is > 0 for every tree n<=26, and tends to 1/sqrt(2pi) with deficit at most about 0.37/V at each member's worst k.

Conclusion (evidence): if N0 is as large as the audits find [wording changed before publication, 2026-09-30, to remove a reference to private correspondence], the obstruction lies in the proof's constants (e.g. c = inf beta/338 in Lemma 6.1, p.10, and the Berry-Esseen step), not in any tree or family approaching failure in the central window. An explicit rate |Q - 1/sqrt(2pi)| <= C/V with V >= c'n would give N0 of order C/(0.4 c'); C ~ 0.4 fits all the data. Newton's inequality itself fails on W5 (min ratio about 0.92), so a real-rootedness route cannot work as stated. delta_k >= 0.9(alpha+1)/((k+1)(alpha-k+1)) held on W5 for every tree seen.
extremal_family: The star K_{1,n-1}: independence polynomial (1+x)^{n-1} + x and delta_k = n/((k+1)(n-k)) for k>=3, minimised at the mode. It gives min central margin 4/(n+2) (n even) or 4n/(n+1)^2 (n odd), ~4/n. It is the unique exhaustive minimiser for 10<=n<=27 and is never beaten by any family member to n~300 or by the hill-climbs. Runners-up are near-stars: a double star, or two stars joined through a midpoint vertex, with n*m -> 4 from above. The known non-log-concave families (Galvin T_{m,t}, Kadrawi-Levit T_{3,m,n}, Bautista-Ramos TG_{m,t}) have central constants of about 8-9 and LC breaks at q+4 or above. For the Newton ratio, the worst shapes are 'star of stars' (a root joined to the centres of several K_{1,3}), at about 0.92.
